newsitem.title: BELGIUM: BELGIAN OLOS TO DRIFT AHEAD U.S. ELECTION RESULTS.
newsitem.headline: BELGIAN OLOS TO DRIFT AHEAD U.S. ELECTION RESULTS.

text.p: Belgian linear bonds (OLOs) lagged Bunds late on Monday as the prospect of Tuesday's U.S. elections drained interest from the market.
And Belgian dealers were divided on whether Tuesday's Treasury exchange auction would re-kindle the market ahead of the results of the first result in U.S. elections in the early hours of Wednesday.
"I can't see the auction doing much," one trader said, noting few dealers still hold paper in OLOs 17 and 22, the two bonds for which the Treasury is offering to swap longer-dated issues.
Another dealer said, however, that because the bonds on offer include an eight and 10-year issue there could be some underperformance in the benchmark 2006.

The 2006 yield rose to 6.14 percent late on Monday from 6.11 percent late on Thursday, when the OLO market closed for an extended holiday weekend. The spread over Bunds widened to 12 basis points from 11.

Most dealers attributed the underperformance, however, to lack of investor interest ahead of the elections. The OLO future also lagged Germany, ending down 0.39 at a session low of 118.89, while the Bund was only slightly lower, they noted.
"There was no demand in the cash or futures market this afternoon. It was very very quiet," one dealer said.
Earlier the OLO curve had flattened sharply in the five to 10-year area as the market played catch up with a sell-off in Bobls on Friday, he said.

The Tresaury on Tuesday is offering OLO lines 17 (6.25 pct November 1996) and 22 (7.50 pct January 1997) against OLOs 10 (8.75 2002), 20 (7.75 pct October 2004), 26 (6.25 pct March 2007) and 23 (8.00 pct March 2015)
